#### AddressClaimRef



AddressClaimRef names the addressing-service claim an assigned address came
from. It is a record, not a lookup: the addressing service is an aggregated
API served on a project control-plane path and defines no CustomResourceDefinition,
so no claim object exists in the cluster a shard runs in and nothing here
resolves one. Reading it means addressing that project's control plane
directly, with a credential a translating node is deliberately not given.

Every field is a plain string and this group depends on no addressing-service
type. The shape matches that service's own opaque cross-API reference, plus
the project, because a claim is namespaced within a project and a namespace
name alone does not identify one from outside.

Populate it with the coordinates of the claim whose allocation produced the
address written alongside it:

	shardAddressIPv6: 2001:db8:f00d::100
	shardAddressIPv6ClaimRef:
	  project: datum-network-edge
	  namespace: egress
	  name: egress-shard-node-a-ipv6

The claim cannot record this relationship itself. The addressing service
overwrites a claim's spec.ownerRef on create with the identity that requested
it, so a claim made by a cell controller is attributed to that controller's
project rather than to the shard it was made for. Attribution therefore runs
in this direction only, and an operator asking which claim holds a shard's
address has this field or nothing.



_Appears in:_
- [EgressShardSpec](#egressshardspec)

#### EgressShard



EgressShard marks a single node as a member of the sharded, stateful egress
translation tier (galactic-nat) — a component deliberately kept off the
ingress load-balancer's own consistent-hash ring (see NetworkGateway):
tenant egress traffic (backend -> arbitrary internet destination) is a
different traffic pattern from ingress (fixed VIP, fixed backend pool)
and needs its own placement ring, own per-flow state, and its own
self-routing return path, entirely independent of any NetworkGateway node.

A shard serves one or both address families. NAT66 (IPv6 -> IPv6) and NAT64
(IPv6 -> IPv4, RFC 6146) are the same function — stateful egress PAT with a
VRF-scoped session table — over different families, so one shard object
describes both rather than there being a second, near-duplicate kind.
Spec.ShardAddressIPv6 and Spec.ShardAddressIPv4 are each assigned only for
the family this shard translates; a shard with no IPv4 address performs no
NAT64.

Every shard owns a dedicated, publicly-routable address per family it
serves, and a flow's allocated masquerade port lives within it — so a reply
is delivered to the correct shard by ordinary unicast routing alone, with
no hashing or cross-shard lookup on the return path at all (the "any node
can determine the owning shard from the tuple alone" property, satisfied by
construction rather than by a replicated hash table).

A shard is told which addresses to translate to; it does not choose them.
The controller that owns a cell claims one address per family from the
addressing service and writes it into this spec, which keeps the
addressing-service credential off every translating node and keeps the
allocation request out of the path that attaches a workload. Status reports
what the node's datapath is actually programmed with, so an unclaimed
address, a stale datapath, and a divergence between the two are each
distinguishable.

A shard names nothing that selects it. Which shards serve which consumer
intent is decided entirely by label selectors evaluated on the selecting
side (see the LabelEgressShard* keys), so no consumer-facing API appears in
this group and no reference points from a datapath resource back at the
resource that placed traffic on it.

#### EgressShardSpec



EgressShardSpec defines the desired state of an EgressShard.

The address fields are written by the controller that owns the cell, not by
the shard and not by a consumer. Each is optional: an address the addressing
service has not yet handed out is absent rather than blank-but-required, so
a shard object exists from the moment its node is labelled and gains its
identity afterwards.

Each is also write-once, and cannot be unassigned once assigned. The
datapath claims a reply by exact match against the address it translates to,
so reassigning one strands the return traffic of every flow already
established through it, with no drain and no dual-address grace period
available to cover the change. A shard holding the wrong address is deleted
and recreated instead, which breaks those flows at a moment someone chose.

A claim reference alongside an address records where that address came from,
and is write-once on the same terms. It is deliberately not required with an
address, in either direction. Requiring an address before a claim reference
would forbid recording a claim whose allocation has not resolved yet, which
is the window a restarting controller most needs to see so that it finds the
claim it already made instead of making a second one. Requiring a claim
reference before an address would forbid an address allocated by hand, and
whether such an address may be recorded here at all is an open migration
question this validation would answer by fiat. An address with no reference
is therefore accepted and is unattributable, which is a fact about the
allocation rather than something a schema can repair.

- [EgressShard](#egressshard)

#### EgressShardStatus



EgressShardStatus defines the observed state of an EgressShard.

The address and prefix fields report what this node's datapath is programmed
with, not what it was asked for. A value here that disagrees with the spec is
a shard that has not converged; a value here with no counterpart in the spec
is a shard still translating to an address nothing assigns any more.

#### NetworkEgressPolicy



NetworkEgressPolicy enables internet egress for a single tenant
VPC/VPCAttachment, served by the sharded, stateful galactic-nat tier
(see EgressShard). Unlike NetworkService, it carries no VIP/backend/port:
egress is on or off for a (vpcRef, vpcAttachmentRef) pair,
existence-implies-enabled, not a per-flow rule — because the destination
of an egress flow is an arbitrary internet address, not a pre-configured
backend list.

It is namespaced (deployed to galactic-system), and RBAC on the namespace
decides who may write it. Like NetworkService's vpcRef, vpcRef and
vpcAttachmentRef are opaque string identifiers because this kind carries
identifiers from the VPC API in api/cloud/v1alpha1 without a Kubernetes
object reference. Galactic does not check that the writer is authorized for
them, and nothing in this repository sets the Accepted condition.

Presence of a NetworkEgressPolicy resolves only *enablement*
(should this tenant's VRF get an egress route toward the shared
translation tier at all) — unlike this type's original design (superseded), there is
no single "assigned gateway node" to compute or pin: any EgressShard may
serve any tenant's flow, chosen by the shard-placement consistent-hash
ring (internal/maglev, keyed on (tenant VRFID, backend, destination) —
see EgressShard's doc comment), not by a per-tenant node assignment stored
here. *Isolation* (preventing two tenants with colliding ULA source
addresses from colliding in the egress connection table) is a separate,
datapath-level concern resolved by tagging each flow with the VRFID
carried in the tenant's own SRv6 Argument, not by anything in this spec.

#### NetworkGateway



NetworkGateway marks a single dedicated gateway-role node as running the
Maglev/DSR consistent-hash L4 load-balancer engine. Exactly one
NetworkGateway exists per gateway node (spec.targetRef.name is the
Kubernetes node name), mirroring the BGPRouter node-scoped root object
pattern. NetworkService resources are served by every NetworkGateway in the
namespace equally (anycast — see NetworkServiceStatus's doc comment); this
object's only job is to identify which nodes participate at all and
surface each node's engine health via Conditions.

This design does no address rewriting on the load-balancing path at all
(DSR — Direct Server Return): the gateway's XDP program picks a backend
via consistent hashing on the flow's 5-tuple and pushes an SRv6 uSID outer
header addressed to the backend's worker node directly, untouched
otherwise. The backend node answers the client directly (see
ServiceVIPBinding) — reply traffic never re-enters this gateway node, so
unlike the Full-NAT design this type originally described, a gateway node
has no SNAT source address of its own to publish and nothing analogous to
sRv6Address/egressAddress/egressSID belongs on this status anymore.

#### NetworkService



NetworkService defines ingress load-balancing for a single tenant VPC, served
by every NetworkGateway node identically (anycast Direct Server Return —
see NetworkGateway's doc comment). vpcRef is an opaque string identifier
because this kind carries identifiers from the VPC API in api/cloud/v1alpha1
without a Kubernetes object reference.

A NetworkService lives in one of two kinds of namespace. In a gateway
namespace, one holding NetworkGateways (galactic-system), it is written by
the platform API that serves tenants, which verifies the tenant owns vpcRef
before it writes the service; RBAC on the namespace decides who else may
write it, and Accepted reports only that a gateway node is registered
there. In a project namespace, one holding no NetworkGateway, it is served
by every NetworkGateway in the cluster and trusted for nothing: it is
Accepted (OwnershipVerified) only while a VPC in its own namespace carries
its vpcRef (OwnershipDenied otherwise), and only while no other service
already serves one of its VIP addresses on its protocol and port
(VIPClaimed); its backends come only from VPCAttachments in its own
namespace. Either way, the BGPAdvertisements and ServiceVIPBindings made for
it live in the gateway namespace.

Unlike the earlier Full-NAT design this type originally described, there
is no primary/secondary gateway node for a service: every NetworkGateway
advertises every accepted service's vipAddresses at equal BGP preference,
consistent-hashes the same backend list to the same backend for the same
flow (internal/maglev), and forwards without rewriting anything —
backend selection never needs a single "owning" node the way Full-NAT's
SNAT-source model did.

Backends are not listed. BackendSelector picks the VPCAttachments that
serve the service, so the backend set follows attachments as they are
created, deleted or moved to another node, and galactic-router on each
node generates the ServiceVIPBinding its backends need from the same
selection.

#### NetworkServiceHealthCheck



NetworkServiceHealthCheck configures the TCP health check of a
NetworkService's backends. A probe succeeds when the TCP handshake completes
within TimeoutSeconds, and fails when the connection is refused, reset or
times out. A backend's decision changes after UnhealthyThreshold consecutive
failures or HealthyThreshold consecutive successes, so a backend that
alternates between the two keeps its current decision.



_Appears in:_
- [NetworkServiceSpec](#networkservicespec)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `failurePolicy` _string_ | FailurePolicy determines whether unknown and all-unhealthy backends may<br />receive traffic. FailClosed requires a current Healthy decision and<br />withdraws the service when health filtering is unavailable. | FailOpen | Enum: [FailOpen FailClosed] <br /> |
| `port` _integer_ | Port is the TCP port probed on every backend, 1-65535. Unset, it is the<br />service's backendPort. A udp service must set it to a TCP port its<br />backends listen on, since a UDP datagram draws no reply a generic<br />probe can expect. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `intervalSeconds` _integer_ | IntervalSeconds is the time between two probes of one backend. | 5 | Maximum: 300 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `timeoutSeconds` _integer_ | TimeoutSeconds is how long a probe waits for the handshake. It must not<br />exceed IntervalSeconds. | 2 | Maximum: 60 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `unhealthyThreshold` _integer_ | UnhealthyThreshold is the number of consecutive failed probes that<br />make a backend Unhealthy. | 3 | Maximum: 10 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `healthyThreshold` _integer_ | HealthyThreshold is the number of consecutive successful probes that<br />make a backend Healthy. | 3 | Maximum: 10 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |


#### NetworkServiceProtocol

_Underlying type:_ _string_

NetworkServiceProtocol is the IP protocol a VIP or endpoint matches.

The set of values is open-ended. A client reading an object that carries
this type must accept a value it does not recognise, preserve it when it
writes the object back, and treat it as a protocol it cannot act on, never
as tcp or udp. Each field of this type admits only the values it lists, and
the API server refuses any other.



_Appears in:_
- [NetworkServiceAddressListener](#networkserviceaddresslistener)
- [NetworkServiceSpec](#networkservicespec)
- [ServiceEndpointSpec](#serviceendpointspec)
- [ServiceRouteProtocolPort](#servicerouteprotocolport)
- [ServiceVIPBindingSpec](#servicevipbindingspec)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `tcp` | NetworkServiceProtocolTCP matches TCP traffic.<br /> |
| `udp` | NetworkServiceProtocolUDP matches UDP traffic.<br /> |
| `sctp` | NetworkServiceProtocolSCTP matches SCTP traffic (IP protocol 132), which<br />has ports. It is declared but not served yet.<br /> |
| `esp` | NetworkServiceProtocolESP matches IPsec Encapsulating Security Payload<br />traffic (IP protocol 50), which has no ports. It is declared but not<br />served yet.<br /> |
| `gre` | NetworkServiceProtocolGRE matches Generic Routing Encapsulation traffic<br />(IP protocol 47), which has no ports. It is declared but not served yet.<br /> |
| `icmp` | NetworkServiceProtocolICMP matches ICMP traffic: ICMPv6 (IP protocol 58)<br />on an IPv6 VIP and ICMP (IP protocol 1) on an IPv4 VIP. It has no ports.<br />It is declared but not served yet.<br /> |


#### NetworkServiceSessionAffinity

_Underlying type:_ _string_

NetworkServiceSessionAffinity selects which parts of a flow a gateway hashes
to pick its backend. Every gateway node hashes a service the same way, so a
flow keeps its backend when it moves between nodes. Affinity is stateless:
it holds only while the backend set is unchanged, and each change to that
set moves about 1/N of clients, N being the number of backends.

_Validation:_
- Enum: [None ClientIP ClientIPAndProtocol]

_Appears in:_
- [NetworkServiceSpec](#networkservicespec)

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | NetworkServiceSessionAffinityNone hashes the client's address and source<br />port, so each connection is balanced on its own.<br /> |
| `ClientIP` | NetworkServiceSessionAffinityClientIP hashes the client's address only,<br />so every connection from one address reaches the same backend, whatever<br />its port, protocol or service among the services sharing that backend<br />set.<br /> |
| `ClientIPAndProtocol` | NetworkServiceSessionAffinityClientIPAndProtocol hashes the client's<br />address and the IP protocol, so every connection from one address over<br />one protocol reaches the same backend, among the services sharing that<br />backend set.<br /> |


#### NetworkServiceSpec



NetworkServiceSpec defines the desired ingress load-balancing state for a
tenant VPC.



_Appears in:_
- [NetworkService](#networkservice)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vpcRef` _string_ | VPCRef is the opaque identifier of the target VPC this service applies<br />to, a VPC's status.vpc. In a gateway namespace, the platform API that<br />serves tenants verifies the tenant owns this VPC before it writes the<br />service. In a project namespace, the service is accepted only while a<br />VPC in that namespace carries this identifier. |  | MinLength: 1 <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `vipAddresses` _string array_ | VIPAddresses is the list of ingress VIP addresses this service provisions<br />on the gateway nodes: at most one IPv6 and at most one IPv4 address.<br />A backend node rewrites a reply's source from the backend's address, port<br />and protocol back to a single VIP of the client's family, so a backend<br />cannot answer for a second VIP of one family. Another VIP of a family<br />needs its own service whose backends listen on a different BackendPort.<br />An IPv4 VIP is written in dotted form; the IPv4-mapped IPv6 form is<br />refused.<br />Workloads are IPv6 only, so both VIPs are served by the selected<br />attachments' IPv6 addresses. A backend node translates the IPv4 VIP's<br />flows statelessly: the backend sees an IPv4 client a.b.c.d as<br />64:ff9b::a.b.c.d (RFC 6052) and replies to that address, and its node<br />sends the reply back to the client as IPv4 from the VIP. A gateway node<br />serves the IPv4 VIP only while it has IPv4 VIPs turned on, and<br />load-balances it only over the backends whose ServiceVIPBinding for it<br />reports Bound. It advertises the IPv4 VIP while at least one such<br />backend exists, and reports the outcome in its "<node>/IPv4Served"<br />condition. The IPv6 VIP is served independently of the IPv4 one.<br />An existing service whose list breaks these limits keeps validating while<br />the list is unchanged, since the API server ratchets validation of an<br />unchanged field on Kubernetes 1.30 and later; any edit to the list must<br />bring it within them, and an older API server refuses any update to such<br />a service. |  | MaxItems: 8 <br />MinItems: 1 <br />Required: \{\} <br />items:MaxLength: 45 <br /> |
| `protocol` _[NetworkServiceProtocol](#networkserviceprotocol)_ | Protocol is the IP protocol this service load-balances on VIPAddresses.<br />The API admits tcp, udp, sctp, esp, gre and icmp, and the gateway<br />datapath serves tcp and udp. A service with any other admitted value is<br />refused with a message saying its protocol is not served yet. sctp has<br />ports and needs Port and BackendPort. esp, gre and icmp have no ports<br />and must set neither; a backend for them is chosen from the client and<br />VIP addresses alone. The set of values is open-ended, so a client must<br />accept and preserve a value it does not recognise, as<br />NetworkServiceProtocol describes. |  | Enum: [tcp udp sctp esp gre icmp] <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `port` _integer_ | Port is the ingress port on VIPAddresses that this service load-balances,<br />1-65535. It is required when PortRange is absent for tcp, udp and sctp<br />and must be unset for one without (esp, gre and icmp). Zero means unset<br />and is omitted when encoding, and an explicit 0 is refused. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `portRange` _[PortRange](#portrange)_ | PortRange replaces Port for an inclusive IPv6 UDP interval. Backend ports<br />are preserved; BackendPort must be omitted. |  |  |
| `addressGroup` _[NetworkServiceAddressGroup](#networkserviceaddressgroup)_ | AddressGroup binds this listener to a complete, authoritative address inventory. |  |  |
| `backendSelector` _[LabelSelector](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v/#labelselector-v1-meta)_ | BackendSelector selects the VPCAttachments (galactic.datumapis.com/v1alpha1)<br />that serve this service, matched against each VPCAttachment object's own<br />labels: in any namespace for a service in a gateway namespace, and only<br />in its own namespace for a service in a project namespace. Only<br />attachments whose status.vpc equals VPCRef are candidates, whatever their<br />labels, so a selector cannot reach into another tenant's VPC. Each selected attachment contributes the<br />IPv6 addresses in its spec.interface.addresses as backends, on<br />BackendPort, for both VIPs: its node translates the IPv4 VIP's flows to<br />and from IPv6, and its IPv4 addresses are never backends. An attachment<br />with no status.node, or no IPv6 address, is not a backend until it has<br />both. An empty selector is rejected rather than read as "every<br />attachment in the VPC". |  | Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `backendPort` _integer_ | BackendPort is the destination port on every selected backend, 1-65535.<br />Like Port, it is required for tcp, udp and sctp and must be unset for<br />esp, gre and icmp. Zero means unset and is omitted when encoding, and an<br />explicit 0 is refused. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `sessionAffinity` _[NetworkServiceSessionAffinity](#networkservicesessionaffinity)_ | SessionAffinity selects which connections from one client share a<br />backend: None, the default, balances each connection on its own;<br />ClientIP pins a client address to one backend; ClientIPAndProtocol pins<br />a client address and protocol to one. Two services pin a client to the<br />same backend only if both set the same affinity and select the same<br />backend addresses. A change takes effect on every gateway node without a<br />restart, and rehashes every connection of the service, so most open<br />connections reach a different backend afterwards. | None | Enum: [None ClientIP ClientIPAndProtocol] <br /> |
| `healthCheck` _[NetworkServiceHealthCheck](#networkservicehealthcheck)_ | HealthCheck turns on health checks for the service's backends. Each<br />backend's own node opens a TCP connection to it on the health check<br />port, from the link-local address of the backend's host-side interface,<br />and publishes a decision in status.health of the backend's<br />ServiceVIPBindings. The gateway nodes take a backend whose decision is<br />Unhealthy out of the service's Maglev table, and keep every backend<br />when all of them are Unhealthy by default. FailClosed instead requires<br />fresh Healthy results for the current configuration and withdraws a VIP<br />with no healthy backends. Unset, no backend is probed and every<br />one stays in the table.<br />Where interface traffic policy is enforced, the backend's policy must<br />allow TCP from fe80::/10 to the health check port on the Private path,<br />and the replies back. |  |  |

#### ServiceEndpointHealthCheck



ServiceEndpointHealthCheck configures the TCP health check of an endpoint's
producers. A probe opens a TCP connection to the producer attachment's first
IPv6 address, not the endpoint's address, on Port, through the producer's
host-side interface and from that interface's link-local address. A producer
with no IPv6 address is never probed and stays Unknown. A probe succeeds when the handshake completes within
TimeoutSeconds, and fails when the connection is refused, reset or times
out. A producer's decision changes after UnhealthyThreshold consecutive
failures or HealthyThreshold consecutive successes. A crashed producer
therefore stops receiving new flows within IntervalSeconds ×
UnhealthyThreshold, plus TimeoutSeconds.



_Appears in:_
- [ServiceEndpointSpec](#serviceendpointspec)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `port` _integer_ | Port is the TCP port probed on every producer, 1-65535. Unset, it is<br />the endpoint's port, which must then be a tcp port. A udp endpoint must<br />set it to a TCP port its producers listen on. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `intervalSeconds` _integer_ | IntervalSeconds is the time between two probes of one producer. | 5 | Maximum: 300 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `timeoutSeconds` _integer_ | TimeoutSeconds is how long a probe waits for the handshake. It must not<br />exceed IntervalSeconds. | 2 | Maximum: 60 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `unhealthyThreshold` _integer_ | UnhealthyThreshold is the number of consecutive failed probes that<br />make a producer Unhealthy. | 3 | Maximum: 10 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `healthyThreshold` _integer_ | HealthyThreshold is the number of consecutive successful probes that<br />make a producer Healthy. | 3 | Maximum: 10 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |

| `node` _string_ | Node is the node that hosts the producer and probes it. |  | MinLength: 1 <br /> |
| `port` _integer_ | Port is the TCP port that was probed. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br /> |
| `state` _[BackendHealthState](#backendhealthstate)_ | State is the decision. Healthy and Unknown producers receive new<br />flows; Unhealthy ones do not, unless every producer on the node is<br />Unhealthy. |  | Enum: [Healthy Unhealthy Unknown] <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `reason` _string_ | Reason is ProbeSucceeded, ProbeFailed, Pending or ProbeUnavailable. |  | MaxLength: 64 <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |

#### ServiceVIPBinding



ServiceVIPBinding drives one worker node's backend-side half of the
DSR/Maglev load-balancer datapath: it tells the node which service VIP a
specific local backend must be reachable on, so the backend can reply to
clients directly (the "Direct Server Return" this design depends on —
see NetworkGateway's doc comment). Generated, never written by users:
galactic-router on each worker node writes one object per (service, VIP,
backend) for every backend a NetworkService's BackendSelector places on that
node, owned by the service, and the same process's per-node reconciler
consumes it.

EgressKind decides which of two backend mechanisms this object drives,
mirroring the same veth/tap fork the SRv6 uSID decap datapath already
has (internal/plumbing/ebpf/usidmap's egress_kind field). Both mechanisms
now converge on the same VIP-boundary substitution
(BackendAddress:BackendPort for VIPAddress:Port at the SRv6 uSID TC-BPF
boundary, usid_ingress's inbound half / usid_egress's outbound half) —
required for both, not just tap, since a decapsulated ingress packet is
delivered into the owning tenant's own VRF routing table, which has no
route to an address bound outside that VRF (found live: see galactic's
ServiceVIPBindingReconciler doc comment):

  - veth (container backend): the node ALSO binds VIPAddress on its own
    galactic-vip0 dummy interface (internal/plumbing/vip's
    Bind/Unbind/Verify in galactic) — this alone does not deliver
    anything to the backend pod (galactic-vip0 lives in the node's root
    namespace, not the tenant's VRF), but still lets the node itself
    verifiably answer on the VIP.
  - tap (VM backend): there is no guest-side configuration capability in
    this repo by design (internal/cnitap's own doc comment), so the
    substitution above is this kind's *only* delivery mechanism — the
    guest OS never needs to know the VIP exists at all.





| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `apiVersion` _string_ | `galactic.datumapis.com/v1alpha1` | | |
| `kind` _string_ | `ServiceVIPBinding` | | |
| `kind` _string_ | Kind is a string value representing the REST resource this object represents.<br />Servers may infer this from the endpoint the client submits requests to.<br />Cannot be updated.<br />In CamelCase.<br />More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#types-kinds |  |  |
| `apiVersion` _string_ | APIVersion defines the versioned schema of this representation of an object.<br />Servers should convert recognized schemas to the latest internal value, and<br />may reject unrecognized values.<br />More info: https://git.k8s.io/community/contributors/devel/sig-architecture/api-conventions.md#resources |  |  |
| `metadata` _[ObjectMeta](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v/#objectmeta-v1-meta)_ | Refer to Kubernetes API documentation for fields of `metadata`. |  |  |
| `spec` _[ServiceVIPBindingSpec](#servicevipbindingspec)_ |  |  |  |
| `status` _[ServiceVIPBindingStatus](#servicevipbindingstatus)_ |  |  |  |

#### ServiceVIPBindingHealth



ServiceVIPBindingHealth is the health decision for a binding's backend. A
decision describes one backend: the VPCAttachment with AttachmentUID, probed
on Port. A reader treats a decision whose attachment UID or port does not
match the backend it is checking as Unknown.



_Appears in:_
- [ServiceVIPBindingStatus](#servicevipbindingstatus)

| Field | Description | Default | Validation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lastProbeTime` _[Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v/#time-v1-meta)_ | LastProbeTime is refreshed after every probe for FailClosed services. |  |  |
| `observedGeneration` _integer_ | ObservedGeneration identifies the NetworkService configuration probed. |  |  |
| `state` _[BackendHealthState](#backendhealthstate)_ | State is the decision. |  | Enum: [Healthy Unhealthy Unknown] <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `reason` _string_ | Reason is ProbeSucceeded, ProbeFailed, Pending or ProbeUnavailable. |  | MaxLength: 64 <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `message` _string_ | Message is the last probe error, when there is one. |  | MaxLength: 1024 <br /> |
| `attachmentUID` _[UID](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v/#uid-types-pkg)_ | AttachmentUID is the UID of the VPCAttachment that held the backend's<br />address when the decision was made. |  | Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `port` _integer_ | Port is the TCP port that was probed. |  | Maximum: 65535 <br />Minimum: 1 <br />Required: \{\} <br /> |
| `lastTransitionTime` _[Time](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/generated/kubernetes-api/v/#time-v1-meta)_ | LastTransitionTime is when State last changed. |  | Required: \{\} <br /> |
